## Parent

Epic `77e3-28e2-31ec-47ec`, authorized at full scope by the operator on 2026-11-02.
Deliverable 1. The calibration corpus (the red proof) is split into child `39bc` because
carrying both exceeds `verify.max_ticket_description_chars`. Citations were measured
individually, not sampled, at `origin/main` `b2dca9bf5ea`.

## The gap

`scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py` is a shrink-only ratchet over
`.github/mechanism-baseline.json` censusing seven mechanism kinds, admitting a new one by
an in-tree marker `# mechanism-ok: <kind> <name> — <reason>`. A `new` key with a nonblank
marker passes (`scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:89-92`), and `parse_marker`
(`scripts/_mechanism_delta/markers.py:37-44`) yields kind, name, reason. Nothing parses a
retirement.

So the ratchet asks "is this mechanism justified?", never "is the system net-simpler
afterward?". Plan review does not close the gap either: `A1`, the only complexity
criterion, is advisory at `"block_threshold": 0.95` / `"default_posture": "advisory"`
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json:814-815`).

This change adds a BLOCKING plan-review criterion, `project.net-mechanism`: a plan adding
a mechanism of a counted kind must either name the mechanism it retires or state why no
retirement is possible, and blocks absent both. It reasons about the PLAN, not the tree:
it runs at claim time, before any code exists.

## Route: project overlay, not a packaged criterion

`project.portability` is a BLOCKING criterion living entirely in the overlay:
`.rebar/criteria_routing.json:3-15` (posture `blocking`, threshold 0.9, `exec: 1-TURN`,
and the declared scope `"applies_at": {"scope": ["container", "leaf"]}`), its `activate`
entry at `:130-132` listing `plan_review`, a rubric under `.rebar/prompts/`, a corpus
under `.rebar/evals/`, and ABSENT from `CANONICAL_LLM` (`registry.py:87`). Five overlay
plan-review criteria ship this way, so the route has precedent.

Chosen because the trigger is rebar's own seven-kind census, which a downstream consumer
lacks: a packaged criterion would fire on their plans. REJECTED and recorded so it is not
re-litigated — packaging it in `CANONICAL_LLM` also costs edits to
`check_registry_coverage` (`registry.py:536`), `validate_packaged_routing()`
(`registry.py:564`) and the regenerated guide (`criteria_guide.py:89`), inviting `A1` on a
complexity-reduction deliverable.

## The rubric's decision logic

The criterion carries no code — its behaviour IS the rubric body, so the body is specified
here, not left to the implementer. Section structure is measured from
`plan-review-project-portability.md`.

**Self-contained taxonomy.** The criterion never reads the ratchet script or baseline: it
runs at claim time against plan prose with no tree access, so it has no runtime source for
the taxonomy. The rubric body must ENUMERATE the closed seven-kind list inline — `lock`,
`env_var`, `config_key`, `feature_flag`, `ci_gate`, `autouse_fixture`, `test_helper` —
each with a one-line cue for recognising it in plan prose, and must state the list is
closed: an element matching none of the seven is not this criterion's concern — that
judgment belongs to `A1`.

**Detection heuristic.** The reviewer extracts, from the plan's stated edit set, every
element it proposes to ADD matching a listed kind and every one it proposes to REMOVE. An
addition is recognised from the plan's declarative statements about what it will create,
not from speculation about what implementation might need.

**Finding threshold** (modeled on `plan-review-project-portability.md:17-37`). Emit only
when ALL of: (1) the plan adds at least one element of a listed kind; (2) it names no
element of those kinds it will retire; (3) it carries no explicit statement of why no
retirement is possible; (4) the addition is specific enough to name a kind and a name.
Condition 4 stops the criterion manufacturing findings from underspecified plans — that is
another criterion's subject.

**Required finding fields** (modeled on `plan-review-project-portability.md:39-54`): five
fields, every one carried by `P1Finding` (`passes.py:50-69`, harvested `:287-300`) —
`location` (the plan section proposing the addition), `finding` (the kind and name added,
plus the absence of both retirement and justification), `scenarios` (one entry per added
kind/name pair — the schema has no `mechanisms` field, so the harvester would drop it;
portability carries its matrix cells in `scenarios` likewise), `evidence` (quoted plan
text), `criteria`.

**Non-findings.** Do NOT emit for: a plan retiring more than it adds; a plan naming a
retirement, even in a different kind; a plan stating why no retirement is possible,
whatever the reviewer thinks of it — the criterion checks the justification is PRESENT,
not persuasive, since judging persuasiveness would make it non-reproducible; a plan adding
no mechanism; a plan adding complexity outside the seven kinds.

## Where firing behaviour is proven

Not here. `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` never executes model
judgment, so a unit test claiming "this plan is scored as a finding" could only assert a
canned score — proving the fixture, not the criterion. This ticket's tests are STRUCTURAL
ONLY; firing behaviour lives in the child's corpus.

The criterion goes live blocking before its firing behaviour is measured. That is safe
because the threshold is CONJUNCTIVE: all four conditions must hold, and condition 2 is
satisfied by any plan naming a retirement, so an uncalibrated rubric of that shape fails
SILENT rather than blocking plans it should pass. The child proves it fires.

## Files this change touches

1. `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-net-mechanism.md` — NEW, the rubric above; front
   matter is the six keys `parse_front_matter` reads.
2. `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — a routing entry and an `activate` entry carrying
   exactly the scope, posture and threshold quoted above. That declared scope —
   `container` and `leaf` tickets under `plan_review` — is the `route_criteria` AC's
   fixture target.
3. `tests/unit/test_project_net_mechanism_criterion.py` — NEW, structural only.

The rubric filename is derived, not chosen: `src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py:42` computes
`f"{prefix}{criterion_id.replace('.', '-')}"`. `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py`
scans the tracked tree against per-file count pins in
`scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt` (`:316-321`), which carries no `.rebar/` row,
so this rubric needs none absent retired vocabulary.

## Portability and provider neutrality

The criterion runs inside plan review, an in-process operation-linked path: it reads plan
text, never the CI environment, so it behaves identically with no CI provider configured.
The `ci_gate` kind concerns what the PLAN says it will add: recognising "a new required
check" in prose needs no CI present. The rubric is `exec: 1-TURN`, names no vendor, and
needs no model-specific capability.

## Acceptance criteria

Each names one deliverable; none bundles two with "and". All are structural, in
`tests/unit/test_project_net_mechanism_criterion.py` bar the last.

- [ ] `registry.effective_criteria(REPO_ROOT)` contains `project.net-mechanism`.
- [ ] `effective_routing(REPO_ROOT)["project.net-mechanism"]["default_posture"]` is
      `"blocking"`.
- [ ] `prompts.get_prompt(criterion_prompt_id("project.net-mechanism"), repo_root=REPO_ROOT)`
      returns a non-empty body.
- [ ] `parse_front_matter` on that body yields all six keys.
- [ ] `route_criteria` returns `project.net-mechanism` for a plan in its declared scope.
- [ ] The rubric body contains a `## Finding threshold` heading.
- [ ] The rubric body contains a `## Required finding fields` heading.
- [ ] The rubric body contains a `## Non-findings` heading.
- [ ] The rubric body names all seven kinds as literal strings.
- [ ] The rubric body contains none of `GitHub Actions`, `GitLab`, `Jenkins`, `CircleCI`,
      `Travis`.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0.
